captions.detailed: A road bike crankset consisting of a light gray cylindrical bottom bracket shell, a black spider chainring with four thin spokes, and two black crank arms oriented in opposite directions. At the end of each crank arm, a silver-colored cylindrical spindle connects to a rectangular black platform pedal. The crank arms and chainring rotate together as a single unit on a continuous revolute joint around the bottom bracket, while each platform pedal rotates independently on its spindle via its own continuous revolute joint.
captions.instruction: Create a 3D model of a road bicycle crankset with a central bottom bracket shell, a spider chainring, and two opposing crank arms. Attach rectangular platform pedals to the ends of the crank arms on spindles, ensuring the main crankset rotates around the bottom bracket and the pedals spin on their own revolute joints.
captions.factory: Construct a fixed base representing the bottom bracket shell using a cylinder primitive. Create the rotating crank assembly (crank arms, axle, and spider chainring) by modeling the chainring with a toothed outer ring and four spokes, then joining it with two elongated crank arms oriented 180 degrees apart. Define a continuous revolute joint between the stationary bottom bracket and this rotating assembly. For the pedals, model rectangular boxes with central spindle cylinders, and establish continuous revolute joints connecting each pedal spindle to its respective crank arm tip.
